\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter06.Pseudorandomness.FourierFourthMoment}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Fourth moment of vector Fourier coefficients]
\lean{FABL.vectorFourierFourthMoment}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p145-b003}
\label{FABL.vectorFourierFourthMoment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff}
For a real-valued function $f$ on the $n$-dimensional cube over $\mathbb{F}_2$, define
its vector Fourier fourth moment to be $\sum_\gamma \widehat f(\gamma)^4$, where
$\widehat f(\gamma)$ denotes the vector Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $\gamma$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Zero frequency and the mean]
\lean{FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_zero_eq_mean}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p026-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p026-b007
}
\proofsource{ghsz-combinatorial-list-decoding}{pdf-6bd33ae73ade-p005-b002}
\label{FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_zero_eq_mean}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.mean, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_eq_expect}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $n$ and every function $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{R}$, the
Fourier coefficient of $f$ at the zero vector equals the mean of $f$ over the cube.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Variance from nonzero Fourier coefficients]
\lean{FABL.variance_eq_sum_sq_vectorFourierCoeff_ne_zero}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p027-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p027-b002
}
\label{FABL.variance_eq_sum_sq_vectorFourierCoeff_ne_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.mean, FABL.variance, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_zero_eq_mean, FABL.vector_plancherel}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f$ be a real-valued function on the binary cube
$(br/2br)^n$. The variance of $f$ under the uniform distribution on this cube equals
the sum of the squares of its vector Fourier coefficients over all nonzero vectors.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourth moment excluding the mean coefficient]
\lean{FABL.vectorFourierFourthMoment_sub_mean_pow_four}
\label{FABL.vectorFourierFourthMoment_sub_mean_pow_four}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.mean, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_zero_eq_mean, FABL.vectorFourierFourthMoment}
\difficulty{4}
For any function $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{R}$, its vector Fourier fourth moment minus
$(\mathbb{E}_x f(x))^4$ equals the sum of the fourth powers of its vector Fourier
coefficients over all nonzero indices $\gamma\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$, where $x$ is uniform on
the cube.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bound on Nonzero Vector Fourier Coefficients]
\lean{FABL.IsFourierRegular.abs_vectorFourierCoeff_le}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p144-b003}
\label{FABL.IsFourierRegular.abs_vectorFourierCoeff_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.IsFourierRegular, FABL.binaryFunctionOnSignCube, FABL.f₂CubeEquivFinset, FABL.f₂Support, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_eq_fourierCoeff_binaryFunctionOnSignCube}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb R$ have the property that every nonempty Fourier
coefficient of the corresponding function on the sign cube has absolute value at most
$\varepsilon$. Then for every nonzero $\gamma\in\mathbb F_2^n$, the vector Fourier
coefficient of $f$ indexed by $\gamma$ has absolute value at most $\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourth moment bound for regular functions]
\lean{FABL.vectorFourierFourthMoment_sub_mean_pow_four_le}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p145-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p145-b004
}
\label{FABL.vectorFourierFourthMoment_sub_mean_pow_four_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.IsFourierRegular, FABL.IsFourierRegular.abs_vectorFourierCoeff_le, FABL.binaryFunctionOnSignCube, FABL.mean, FABL.variance, FABL.variance_eq_sum_sq_vectorFourierCoeff_ne_zero, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff, FABL.vectorFourierFourthMoment, FABL.vectorFourierFourthMoment_sub_mean_pow_four}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{R}$ and let $\varepsilon\in\mathbb{R}$. If the function
on the sign cube obtained from $f$ through the coordinatewise binary-to-sign bijection
has every nonempty Fourier coefficient bounded in absolute value by $\varepsilon$, then
the vector Fourier fourth moment of $f$ minus $(\mathbb{E}f)^4$ is at most
$\varepsilon^2\operatorname{Var}(f)$, with the mean and variance taken under the uniform
distribution on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Large coefficient from irregularity]
\lean{FABL.exists_abs_vectorFourierCoeff_gt_of_not_isFourierRegular}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p144-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p145-b004
}
\label{FABL.exists_abs_vectorFourierCoeff_gt_of_not_isFourierRegular}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.IsFourierRegular, FABL.binaryFunctionOnSignCube, FABL.f₂CubeEquivFinset, FABL.f₂Support, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_eq_fourierCoeff_binaryFunctionOnSignCube}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb R$. If the function
on the sign cube obtained by transporting $f$ through the coordinatewise sign encoding
is not Fourier regular at level $\varepsilon$, then there is a nonzero $\gamma\in\mathbb
F_2^n$ such that $\varepsilon<|\widehat f(\gamma)|$, where $\widehat f(\gamma)$ is the
vector Fourier coefficient of $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourth moment bound from Fourier irregularity]
\lean{FABL.epsilon_pow_four_le_vectorFourierFourthMoment_sub_mean_pow_four}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p145-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p145-b004
}
\label{FABL.epsilon_pow_four_le_vectorFourierFourthMoment_sub_mean_pow_four}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.IsFourierRegular, FABL.binaryFunctionOnSignCube, FABL.exists_abs_vectorFourierCoeff_gt_of_not_isFourierRegular, FABL.mean, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff, FABL.vectorFourierFourthMoment, FABL.vectorFourierFourthMoment_sub_mean_pow_four}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb R$. Suppose
$\epsilon\ge0$ and that there is a nonempty set of coordinates whose Fourier coefficient
for the corresponding sign-cube representation of $f$ has absolute value greater than
$\epsilon$. Then $\epsilon^4\le \sum_{\gamma\in\mathbb F_2^n}\widehat
f(\gamma)^4-(\mathbb E f)^4$, where $\widehat f(\gamma)$ denotes the Fourier coefficient
indexed by $\gamma$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficient of a convolution]
\lean{FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_convolution}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p030-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p030-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p030-b006
}
\label{FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_convolution}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.binaryFourierCoeff_convolution, FABL.convolution, FABL.f₂Support, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff}
\difficulty{1}
Let $f,g\colon\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb R$ and $\gamma\in\mathbb F_2^n$. The vector
Fourier coefficient of the convolution of $f$ and $g$ at $\gamma$ equals the product of
their vector Fourier coefficients at $\gamma$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourth Fourier moment and convolution]
\lean{FABL.vectorFourierFourthMoment_eq_expect_convolution_mul_self}
\label{FABL.vectorFourierFourthMoment_eq_expect_convolution_mul_self}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.convolution, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_convolution, FABL.vectorFourierFourthMoment, FABL.vector_plancherel}
\difficulty{3}
For any function $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{R}$, the sum of the fourth powers of its
vector Fourier coefficients equals $\mathbb{E}_t[(f*f)(t)^2]$, where $t$ is uniform on
$\mathbb{F}_2^n$ and $f*f$ denotes the normalized convolution of $f$ with itself.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Convolution and additive energy]
\lean{FABL.expect_convolution_mul_self_eq_additiveEnergy}
\label{FABL.expect_convolution_mul_self_eq_additiveEnergy}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.convolution, FABL.convolution_apply_add}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:(\\mathbb F_2)^n\\to\\mathbb R$. The uniform
average over $t\\in(\\mathbb F_2)^n$ of the square of the normalized additive
convolution $f*f(t)$ equals $\\mathbb E_{x,y,z}\\, f(x)f(y)f(z)f(x+y+z)$, where $x,y,z$
are independent uniform elements of $(\\mathbb F_2)^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourth Fourier moment and additive energy]
\lean{FABL.vectorFourierFourthMoment_eq_additiveEnergy}
\label{FABL.vectorFourierFourthMoment_eq_additiveEnergy}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.expect_convolution_mul_self_eq_additiveEnergy, FABL.vectorFourierFourthMoment, FABL.vectorFourierFourthMoment_eq_expect_convolution_mul_self}
\difficulty{1}
For any function $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{R}$, the sum of the fourth powers of its
vector Fourier coefficients equals $\mathbb{E}_{x,y,z}[f(x)f(y)f(z)f(x+y+z)]$, where
$x,y,z$ are independent uniform points of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$.
\end{theorem}
